A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SpikeStereoNet and the same underlying datasets and architecture. Inspection of all 26 pages of v2 and 31 pages of v3, including rendered figures, tables, equations, and appendices, supports reliable comparison across additions and relocations.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic and real-data evaluations, data-efficiency experiments, network-dynamics analyses, and appendix ablations, including Tables 1–9.

after.justification: v3 retains original evaluations and adds reported sensitivity, synchronization, computational-efficiency, and hybrid-fusion results.

M1.justification: The core feature extraction, correlation pyramid, adaptive RSNN update, and loss remain unchanged. Appendix A.5.5 adds preliminary architecture adaptations: a TFI feature branch and RGB early/context fusion. These extend the method with optional hybrid-input variants.

E1.justification: The synthetic scenes and indoor real dataset are retained. v3 additionally evaluates depth estimation using Kinect RGB frames together with spikes, introducing a hybrid sensor-input scenario in Table 9. The proposed outdoor and broader object collections remain future work in both versions.

E2.justification: The synthetic comparison retains the same ten baselines. The real comparison expands from v2 Table 4 to v3 Table 2 by adding IGEV-Stereo and Mocha-stereo. v3 Table 4 also adds GRU and LSTM update-block comparisons; RNN and fixed-LIF controls already existed in v2.

E3.justification: New protocols cover threshold multipliers of 0.7–1.6, temporal steps of 0.5–4 ms, fusion windows of 10/30/50, and comparative timing on an RTX 3090 using T=50. Appendix A.2.7 also qualifies v2's common-settings description with baseline-specific tuning and validation-based selection. The principal training budget and dataset splits remain unchanged; these descriptions do not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds threshold/temporal-quantization sensitivity, synchronization-offset analysis, and hybrid-fusion controls, and expands neuron replacements with GRU/LSTM. It also revises the regularization controls to distinguish voltage and firing-rate removal. The earlier fixed-LIF, RNN/GN, iteration-count, and interpolation analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: v3 first specifies averaging over 100 inference runs for the new timing comparison and reports a Gaussian model with mean and dispersion for synchronization offsets. Fixed-seed statements and the existing PSNR/SSIM uncertainty reports are retained; no new accuracy confidence intervals or repeated-training-seed analysis appears.

E6.justification: Main synthetic scores and retained real-data rows are unchanged, including the model's AvgErr of 0.42 and 0.56 px. v3 adds sensitivity, timing, synchronization, fusion, and comparator results. Table 9 reports RGB fusion at 5.08% bad-2.0 and 0.59 px AvgErr versus 5.33% and 0.56 px for spike-only. The no-GN row changes from 7.33/2.97/0.57 to 7.49/3.11/0.58, and several regularization results are reassigned to different conditions.

T1.justification: v3 adds formal synchronization-offset definitions, a Gaussian jitter assumption, and temporal-correlation alignment equations in A.4.3, plus hybrid accumulation and raw-SNN equations. The principal neuron/loss equations and the contraction and fixed-point argument in A.5.1 retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: v3 removes the claims of being the first raw-spike stereo framework and the first corresponding large-scale datasets from the abstract and contribution statements. The main claims concerning RSNN refinement, accuracy, stability, and data efficiency are retained.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations attributing threshold/timing robustness to adaptive gates, recurrence, and regularization. It discusses hybrid fusion's structural benefits and limitations from noise, temporal lag, alignment, and HDR mismatch. The existing limitations concerning real-data scale and the synthetic-to-real gap are preserved, moved to A.6.

D1.justification: New appendix sections document baseline tuning ranges and selection, camera synchronization, LED-based offset estimation, temporal alignment, and jitter simulation. v3 also specifies the 16 mm focal length, timing hardware, fusion implementation, and a repository link. These substantially expand reproducibility information; the PDFs do not verify repository contents, and release statements remain prospective.

R1.justification: The introduction substantially expands positioning around spiking-neuron models, surrogate-gradient training, adaptive recurrent SNNs, and biologically inspired vision. Related work newly acknowledges Wang et al. (2022) on spike-camera stereo depth, alongside the narrowed priority claims. Additional optical-flow and hybrid-sensing literature also appears; publication updates to retained references are not counted as new works.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the overall section hierarchy are preserved. Local restructuring brings real-data results and expanded neuron ablations into the main text and moves limitations to the appendix. v3 adds focused explanatory subsections, updates affiliations/header text, adds acknowledgments, and standardizes references.

P2.justification: v3 adds four tables for sensitivity, comparative timing, TFI fusion, and RGB fusion. It restructures the architecture ablation table, consolidates and expands neuron comparisons, and relocates the expanded real-data table into the main text. All thirteen existing figures remain, with changes to placement, grouping, and limited caption wording.

improvement.justification: v3 improves evaluability through additional controls, broader real-data comparisons, synchronization and tuning documentation, and more careful novelty positioning. The core results and proof remain stable. Reporting problems limit the gain: A.5.3 claims threshold variation within 5.9% although Table 6 lists 8.3%, and revised regularization labels are not fully reconciled with the accompanying discussion. The additions support a limited overall improvement rather than resolving all evidential weaknesses.
